messages:
Maria: Ran a focused nsys trace on the nightly kv-refill run after the tail spikes report. Timeline shows long H2D slices blocking small latency kernels; suspect pageable host staging.
Kevin: which capture flags did you use? can you re-run with host pinned buffers to compare?
Maria: capture command (simplified): `nsys profile -o /tmp/kv_refill --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none ./redwood-server --bench refill` Attached zoomed timeline and top api/cuda events.
Maria: Observed pattern: repeated `cudaMemcpyAsync` H2D slices ~80-150ms (varies), interspersed with tiny kernels (1-6ms) that end up queued until copy returns. Multiple concurrent refills from different streams.
Sanjay: 80-150ms is classic pageable fallback. Any indication of `cuHostRegister` or explicit pinned allocs?
Maria: No, refill path currently uses malloc->cudaMemcpyAsync. nsys shows the copies flagged as pageable fallback. Also saw occasional `cuMemcpyPeer` when both GPUs share NVLink but often host staging is used.
Alex: If the refill allocator returns pageable buffers, peercopy will fallback to host copy. Might explain inconsistent peercopy behavior. Also check that we call `cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess` at init for pairs.
Kevin: quick test: switch refill staging to pinned via `cudaHostAlloc` or `cudaHostRegister` and re-run. If the H2D time drops to ~10-20ms, that's strong evidence.
Maria: Ran that test. Repro script `ci/perf/kv_h2d_probe.py` toggles pinned vs pageable. Results saved to /tmp/kv_h2d_results.csv. Summary: pageable 95-140ms, pinned 9-18ms for 32MB transfers.
perf-bot: note: perf-run-1774056790/pinned-compare attached to perf dashboard.
Sanjay: Nice. Two follow-ups: (1) why are multiple refills concurrent? batching heuristic might be spawning them in parallel; (2) verify we aren't synchronizing streams accidentally.
Maria: Found an extra `cudaStreamSynchronize` in refill hotpath inside an error-check block. That causes unexpected blocking when two refills happen. Removing that reduces interleaving.
Alex: For batching heuristics: we're launching refill for each request when prefix cache miss occurs. We could coalesce where multiple requests ask for overlapping prefixes within 10ms window and do one larger copy. Also put a soft cap on concurrent refills (e.g., 4).
Kevin: Also consider using GPUDirect P2P when possible (cudaMemcpyPeerAsync). NVLink peercopy is fastest but only works when both devices in same PCI root complex and peer access enabled. For cross-socket or network cases, prefer pinned host staging.
Maria: Added runtime checks: on init run `cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer` for device pairs and call `cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess` where true. Also ensured KV cache entries store GPU pointers when resident so future refills can do direct peercopy.
Sanjay: Good. Another observation from nsys: some memcpy slices show heavy syscall time on the host side (pageable faulting causing page-in). That explains variability. Pinned removes page-fault cost.
Alex: We should instrument the runtime logs to emit a short tag when a refill used peercopy vs hostcopy vs pageable fallback. That will help in production triage.
Maria: Plan/PRs: (1) eng-runtime: implement pinned staging behind FF and add a fallback path (Maria) (2) runtime: coalesce refills + concurrent-refill throttle (Alex) (3) perf: run cluster-wide pinned vs baseline comparison and add the repro script to CI (Sanjay).
Kevin: Also add a non-blocking backpressure in the batching intake: if concurrent refills >= 4, slow acceptance of new requests or prioritize in-memory hits.
Maria: Quick note: when testing multi-GPU on node, `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync` gives ~6-12ms for 32MB, but only if source/dest buffers are pinned/GPU-resident. If not, it falls back to host copy costing ~100ms.
perf-bot: reminder: tag tests with GPU topology info (node id, pcie root, nvlink presence) so we can correlate.
Maria: I'll open PR for pinned path + small perf harness. Will include `nsys` snippet and script to reproduce.
Alex: Great work. This aligns with the hypothesis that pageable staging + concurrent refills cause the tail spikes and tiny kernel launches amplify the impact.
Kevin: once PR is up, perf run and let's gate on tail latency improvement. Add log tags as mentioned.
Maria: will do. Thanks! :thumbsup:
